argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy the release-policy predicate for an exposed weak segment. It does support a narrower certification posture: aggregate launch readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, deployment is limited to 6% with rollback and monitoring, and the audit packet can accurately preserve that the claims subrogation review segment remains below target and exposed. On that record, the strongest supportable position is not full policy cure, but certification with an explicit disclosed limitation and a caveat that controls manage deployment risk while the exposure remains visible on the record.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only risk-managed reading of this record because the release already has aggregate readiness clearance, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, reversibility, and active monitoring. A bounded caveat preserves launch governance without overstating compliance and avoids treating the operational controls as worthless where they do materially reduce deployment risk.
claims_about_policy: The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record shows neither exclusion of the claims subrogation review segment nor approved risk acceptance expressly covering that exposure. Accordingly, rollback, monitoring, and limited rollout percentage should be presented as operational risk controls, not as eliminating the disclosure duty or fully satisfying the mitigation condition.
concessions: The claims subrogation review segment remains below target and is still eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The current risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver signature, and does not expressly cover subrogation exposure.
Public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance supports disclosure and monitoring, but does not replace the case-specific policy condition.
